name: Diazepam
summary: A long-acting benzodiazepine with active metabolites, widely used for alcohol withdrawal, seizures, and muscle spasm.
mechanism: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors, enhancing inhibitory GABAergic transmission.

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: ~20–80 h (parent); active metabolites persist for days
pharmacokinetics.duration: Long — 24 h+, with cumulative active metabolites
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 to active metabolite desmethyldiazepam

dosing.adult: 2–10 mg two to four times daily (usual 4–40 mg/day); 5–10 mg IV for status epilepticus or alcohol withdrawal

safety.pregnancy: Avoid; floppy infant syndrome and neonatal withdrawal with late-pregnancy use.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; infant sedation possible.
contraindications: Severe respiratory insufficiency or sleep apnea
warnings: Boxed warning: dependence, abuse, and withdrawal with long-term use
Boxed warning: respiratory depression when combined with opioids
Accumulation in the elderly (long half-life plus active metabolites) — falls and oversedation
monitoring: Sedation and accumulation in the elderly
safety.overdose: Prolonged sedation and respiratory depression; effects can persist for days due to active metabolites; flumazenil reversal.

clinicalPearls: Active metabolites give a half-life of days — accumulates quickly in the elderly; use the lowest effective dose.
Standard agent for alcohol withdrawal and muscle spasm; IM absorption is erratic — prefer oral or IV.
good: Alcohol withdrawal, status epilepticus, or muscle spasm where a long-acting BZD is standard.
bad: Elderly patients (accumulation), respiratory disease, or long-term daily use.
